problem: ns-gm is the execution vehicle for NetSuite record changes in execute mode. The RESTlet currently supports arbitrary SuiteScript execution but has no approval intercept mechanism. The ticket proposes a beforeSubmit UserEventScript that checks with Helix mainland before allowing record saves — this would be a new SuiteScript deployment alongside the existing RESTlet.

files.why: The NetSuite RESTlet that executes arbitrary SuiteScript 2.1 code via new Function(). Currently handles 'run' and 'getscriptexecutionlogs' actions. This is the primary execution vehicle — scripts proposed by the agent would be run through this RESTlet. Lines 45-154 handle code execution with all 24 N/* modules injected.
Local Express proxy with /run and /logs endpoints. Scripts are sent to NetSuite via POST /run. Execute mode would use this same pathway to submit approved scripts.
OAuth 2.0 M2M authentication for RESTlet access. Same auth mechanism needed for any new NetSuite scripts (beforeSubmit, Suitelet) that need to call back to Helix.
CLI run command that sends code to proxy. Shows the execution flow from CLI -> proxy -> RESTlet. Execute mode's deterministic program would follow a similar code submission path.
Configuration loader (port, settings). May need extension for execute-mode-specific config.
Project identity and architecture documentation. Core architecture: CLI -> local Express proxy -> NetSuite RESTlet.
Product definition for ns-gm. Establishes the tool's purpose and user base.
Dependencies (axios, commander, express, jose). No database, no ORM, no build step, no test commands.

facts: ns-gm RESTlet executes arbitrary SuiteScript 2.1 via new Function() with 24 injected N/* modules including N/record, N/transaction, N/workflow (ns_gm_restlet.js line 166)
RESTlet only handles two actions: 'run' (execute code) and 'getscriptexecutionlogs' (retrieve logs). No approval, intercept, or validation actions exist.
The RESTlet is deployed as @NScriptType Restlet with @NModuleScope Public (ns_gm_restlet.js lines 2-4)
Local proxy runs on port 9292 (configurable) with Express. Endpoints: GET /health, POST /run, POST /logs (server/app.js)
Authentication is OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials with JWT client assertion using PS256 (server/auth.js)
ns-gm has no communication channel back to Helix mainland server — all communication is outbound to NetSuite
No database, no ORM, no migrations. Credential storage is file-based (~/.ns-gm/credentials.json)
No build step (raw JS), no test commands. Only eslint and prettier as dev dependencies.
The RESTlet returns execution result, execution time, and governance metrics (remaining usage units)
The ns-gm CLI is installed in Helix workflow sandboxes via installNsGmCli (referenced in helix-global-server orchestrator)
